## Spec conformance

SPEC §3 T21: *"`frame_work.js`; legacy 6 ms families register as W6 clients under the global cap (code unchanged). Acceptance: GATE-PHASE — `__framePhase` census (re-classes the [A] phase budgets); BENCH-CROSS-SETTLE fast-line AND 666 (the under-serving risk; named lever = CROSSING elevated mode before killing). Kill: K2 — boot-to-in-world or crossing-settle regression beyond noise on interleaved arms."*

- **`frame_work.js` per pass 8 (single post-render stream slot, 6 ms global budget, priority classes, always-run-one, BOOT/TELEPORT/EMERGENCY modes, starvation counters)** — **MET.** All S2 rules implemented and unit-pinned (144 checks, mocked clock). The slot runs post-render inside the same rAF task at every exit path (incl. the direct path's F4 finally and the nullRender bot exit); alternate drivers run P4 per S1. CROSSING implemented as the pre-declared lever behind `?workCrossing` (default OFF). EMERGENCY has its full reweight semantics but no stage-A producer (the pressure ladder is T20's; `setEmergency()` is its seam) — stated, not simulated.
- **Legacy 6 ms families as W6 clients, code unchanged** — **MET.** All six family sites read-verified and registered: `statics.js:2233/3052` (both loops + walkInInstance pass 2), `cells.js:917`, `buildings.js:178`, `landblock_lru.js:44/356` (both inside `tickEviction`, which registers as one coalesced W6 run from index.js), `xu7_textures.js` FIFO drain, plus the un-budgeted inline `tickEviction` itself. Every adapter is one line at the existing yield/schedule seam; every internal loop, budget constant, and cancellation guard is untouched.
- **Flag-off byte-identical (I7)** — **MET.** OFF arm: `frameWorkW6Yield` returns exactly the old `new Promise(r => setTimeout(r, 0))`; `frameWorkW6Run` declines and callers fall through to their verbatim legacy scheduling; the P4 helper and phase marks are guarded no-ops; no `await` shape changed on the OFF path (the post-render helper is synchronous when OFF). All pre-existing suites over the touched families green (below).
- **`__framePhase` census surface** — **MET.** Implemented per the registry's reserved schema (last-frame levels + cumulative counters + frames), stamped into the pass-08 S1 taxonomy applied to today's frame order; independent of `?frameWork` so the census can measure the legacy arm (where p4 ≈ 0 and between-frames family work is invisible — the asymmetry the census exists to show). Granted W6 continuations are measured inside p4 (one-microtask hop before the cut).
- **`__frameWork` diag (per-class served/starved/budget counters)** — **MET.** Registry-conformant rows W1..W6 (`ran`/`deferredFrames`/`forcedRuns`/`maxItemMs`/`queueDepth`/`itemsThisFrame`), `mode` level, `budgetMs`, `teleports`, `guardServices`, stage-C `uploads` shape (zeros). Installed at module scope so flag-OFF runs read `enabled:false` zeros (the `__texWorkerStats` convention).

## Deviations

None against SPEC.md. Four sub-spec notes (refinements within the contract, per I3's spirit):

1. **Inline `tickEviction` registered at stage A.** Pass-08 H-08.1 sequences "P4 relocation of eviction/feeds" as stage two; the T21 assignment (and SPEC's stage-A W6 sentence) explicitly lists the un-budgeted inline `tickEviction` among the stage-A registrants. Implemented as the assignment directs, in the thinnest form: the CALL moves under the slot (coalesced, latest args), the LRU code does not change at all. The full event-driven eviction relocation (grid events → W4 drains) remains T20/T22 scope.
2. **BOOT-mode exit predicate.** Pass-08 S1 says "BOOT mode ends at `preview-complete`"; that milestone does not exist pre-ST2. Stage A uses `window.__bootState === "in-world"` — pass-08 D-08.3's own "pre-`in-world`" wording — one-way, with `notifyInWorld()` as the explicit seam. The ST2+ milestone takes over when it exists.
3. **W6 resume grants are estimate-charged.** A granted chunk continuation executes in the microtask drain after `run()` returns, so its cost cannot be measured synchronously inside the slot. Grants are charged at the family's last reported chunk ms (clamped 0.5–50, default the house 6); the real cost arrives at the next `w6Yield(name, spentMs)` and feeds `maxItemMs` + the next estimate. `__framePhase.p4` measures the true execution (the one-microtask hop) — so the estimate only steers admission, never the record.
4. **7 phase marks, not "5 paired reads".** Pass-08 S7 modeled 5 reads for the reordered end-state frame; today's tick interleaves the LRU block between two P2 spans, so the stage-A census takes 7 marks (p2 accumulates two segments). Same vector, same semantics; the reads are flag-gated to zero on bare defaults.

One I2 out-of-scope edit, recorded: `scene3d/stall_probe.js` (+33 lines, additive guarded reads) — pass-08 S7.3 binds the probe's `_sample` extension to the same landing as the surfaces ("instrument wiring is doc-propagation duty"); leaving it out would have shipped the surfaces in violation of that rule. Commit `80761d45` carries the note.

## Handoffs & risks

- **GATE-PHASE runs (orchestrator / next low-memory window):** the census is one command per arm once a headless session is affordable (runbook in "Spec conformance" above and in the census header). Run the LEGACY arm first — it is the [A]-re-class evidence; the `?frameWork=on` arm additionally shows p4 occupancy + W6 counters.
- **BENCH-CROSS-SETTLE (1070 batch cadence):** arms `?frameWork=off|on` (+`&workCrossing=on` as the repair arm), interleaved, fast-line AND 666. Under-serving evidence = `__frameWork.classes.W6.deferredFrames`/`forcedRuns` climbing during crossings + settle-time regression. The kill is one flag; the lever is pulled before the kill (§0 row).
- **T22 (stages B/C) consumes:** `enqueue(classId, {kind, fn, bytes, tileKey})`, `purgeByTile`, the W2/W3 byte-cap seam (not yet enforced — D-08.5 caps belong to the upload/feed producers T22 lands), the `uploads` surface shape, and the P4 site. The one-microtask-hop p4 measurement pattern extends to W3 feed execution unchanged.
- **T20 consumes:** `setEmergency()` (ladder R4), `notifyInWorld()`, and should replace `noteLbKey`'s Chebyshev heuristic with real grid `onTeleport` events at ST7.
- **Risk — estimate charging:** a family whose chunk cost varies wildly frame-to-frame is admission-steered by its previous chunk (clamped 0.5–50 ms). Bounded by construction (always-run-one + 3-frame ceiling guarantee service); the census + `maxItemMs` will show if a tighter estimator is needed.
- **Risk — throughput under the global cap:** with `?frameWork=on`, NORMAL mode serves roughly one legacy chunk per frame where the additive families could run ~5× that between frames. This is the DESIGNED trade (tail bounds over peak throughput) and exactly what BENCH-CROSS-SETTLE scores; BOOT (50 ms) + the guard's setTimeout(0) chain keep boot-time throughput at today's cadence, and CROSSING is the standing repair.
- **Observation for the orchestrator (not T21's to fix):** IMPLEMENTATION.md I4 says `dist` → `/mnt/wbterminal2/holtburger-dist-hires-bc7m-xu7t2`; the live symlink reads `/mnt/wbterminal2/holtburger-dist-hires-bc7m-xu7` (no `t2`). serve.py serves 200 either way; flagging the doc/reality skew.
- **Pre-existing reds** (unchanged by T21, listed in Tests run): lint-url-flags --strict 2 presence-guard findings; test_envcell_guard splice failure; run-all --js 17-unregistered-suites (T01's finding).
